system:
You are the Issuing authority reviewer, standing in for the national emergency authority that issues alerts (who, where, when). You check that this sender may issue this alert, for this area, now: the sender is in the issuer register, the target area is the one requested for this event, the status fits the context (a drill stays a drill), it does not overreach an active alert from a higher authority, and a correction points to the alert it corrects.
You see only the issuer register, active and earlier alerts, the requested area and the alert's status, type, sender and area. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

For every objection also fill `uae_basis`: if one of the UAE clauses shown (ids starting with ITU-UAE:, TDRA-,
UAE-, DXB-) speaks to this issue, set status "cites_uae" with its id and a word-for-word quote; otherwise set
status "none_applies" with empty ref and quote. Say "none_applies" honestly: it tells the regulator where UAE
texts are silent.

FCC 16-127 Matching the Geographic Target Area a. Background 138. While our geo-targeting requirement, as amended above, will improve WEA geotargeting by facilitating the delivery of Alert Messages to a more granular polygon level, the limitations of cell broadcast-based geo-targeting may result in continued over-alerting.573 According to CSRIC IV, the “ideal case” from an alert originator perspective would be where “all WEA-enabled mobile devices in the geographic area affected by an emergency event would receive the WEA Alert Message broadcast, and no mobile devices outside the defined alert area would receive those particular WEA Alert Message broadcasts.”574 “However,” CSRIC IV reports, “this ideal case cannot be realized using currently deployed cell broadcast alone.”575 CSRIC V recommends that the Commission collaborate with WEA stakeholders to develop standards and implement systems that support enhanced, device-based geotargeting.576 CSRIC V recommends that the Commission set a goal that Participating CMS Providers geo-target Alert Messages in a manner that includes “100% of the targeted devices within the specified alert area with not more than .10 mile overshoot,” and states that WEA stakeholders, including Participating CMS Providers, “have committed to working to close the gap between current capabilities and aspirational goals.”577 b. A device-based solution entails an alert originator transmitting geographic coordinates for the target area along with the WEA message, and an end-user device using the device’s location-based technology to display only those WEA messages that are relevant to the geographic area in which the device is located. CSRIC IV WEA Messaging Report at 40. This technique is sometimes referred to as “geo-fencing.” See, e.g., NWS May 21, 2015 Ex Parte Letter at 2. FEMA agrees that “[g]eo-targeting proficiency can be improved by implementing geographical targeting for WEA broadcasts by cell-sector, including delivery of alert area specifications to the phone enabling mobile-assisted geographical targeting (aka geo-fencing), and other techniques.” FEMA Jun 18 Ex Parte Letter at 2. 218 CSRIC V, Working Group Two, Wireless Emergency Alerts – Recommendations to Improve Geo-Targeting and Offer Many-to-One Capabilities, Final Report, at 30 (2016) (CSRIC V WEA Geo-targeting Report). 219 [FCC-16-127#0207] Wireless Emergency Alerts; Amendments to Part 11 Regarding the Emergency Alert System, Report and Order and FNPRM (FCC 16-127) (p.35): Narrowing Geo-targeting Requirements a. Background 50. Under Section 10.450 of the Commission’s WEA rules, Participating CMS Providers may not transmit Alert Messages to areas larger than the county or county equivalents with which the target area of the Alert Message overlaps.210 In the WEA First Report and Order, we concluded that it would be premature to require geo-targeting to areas smaller than a county, despite many commenters’ statements that cell broadcast technology could already support geo-targeting at the sub-county level, because not all carriers were expected to employ cell broadcast to deliver Alert Messages, and because NWS was currently only targeting its Alert Messages at the county level.211 In the WEA NPRM, we proposed to narrow our WEA geo-targeting requirement such that any Alert Message that is specified by a geocode, circle, or polygon must be transmitted to an area not larger than the specified area.212 If, however, a Participating CMS Provider is unable to accurately match the geocode, circle, or polygon provided by the emergency manager, we proposed to retain the current backstop that the Participating CMS Provider may geo-target the Alert Message to an area that approximates the desired alert area, but is no larger than a single transmission site.213 51. This will effectively eliminate the effect of overshoot of the radio signal for cell broadcast outside the targeted warning notification area. DBGF is specified in ETSI TS 123 041 [1] for E-UTRAN and NG-RAN. EU-Alert shall support DBGF. data.summary: Seoul Metropolitan Government (level 2) is registered only for Seoul (KR-ADM=11 and its polygon). The alert targets Seoul, but the area requested for this event is Baengnyeong-myeon and Daecheong-myeon in Ongjin-gun, Incheon (KR-ADM 28720), which is the area in the Ministry of the Interior and Safety's active level-1 air-raid alert. The alert's area does not match the requested area. The sender is also not authorised for 28720. Issuing an Actual air-raid alert for all of Seoul would go beyond the sender's remit for this event and duplicate a higher authority's alert for a different area. The drafter should retarget to the requested area, but this sender cannot cover it, so the alert should go to the Ministry or be authorised by it.

objections.issue: Alert area (Seoul, KR-ADM 11 with polygon) is not the area requested for this event (Ongjin-gun, KR-ADM 28720, named in the ministry's alert). An Actual air-raid alert for a different area would alarm the whole of Seoul, which is not under threat.
objections.fix: Replace the area with the requested area (KR-ADM 28720) and remove the Seoul code and polygon. Because Seoul is not authorised for 28720, this alert should be issued by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety or with its authorisation. Otherwise withdraw the draft.

objections.issue: The sender is outside its registered jurisdiction. Seoul Metropolitan Government is registered only for KR-ADM=11 and the Seoul polygon, and the Ministry's active level-1 air-raid alert already covers 28720. Seoul has no authority over Ongjin-gun, and issuing its own Actual air-raid alert risks conflicting with or overreaching the higher authority's alert.
objections.fix: Do not issue this alert from Seoul for Incheon area 28720. Defer to the Ministry's active alert, or have the Ministry issue it. If Seoul itself faces a separate threat, obtain the Ministry's confirmation first.
